items.headline: Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy
items.blurb: The US president said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him about the affair with the alleged spy.
items.text: Donald Trump has said the boss of Nvidia, whose affair with an alleged Chinese spy is being investigated, told him that he had "no idea she was a spy". The US President said he spoke with CEO Jensen Huang on Monday following reports that the US believed he had been targeted in a Chinese espionage campaign. "I asked him that question, 'Did you have any idea she was a spy?' He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters. Trump said the FBI was also investigating the affair. China has rejected claims that Huang was targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China". Nvidia, who commissioned an independent investigation into the affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy, said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised. items.headline: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven
items.blurb: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.
items.text: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said. The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry. An inspection indicated that the Cairo-Aswan train had been stationary on the same track, officials said. The health ministry gave the casualty toll, adding more than 70 of the injured were discharged after receiving treatment. Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. In recent years the government has announced modernisation initiatives to improve its railways. items.headline: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
items.blurb: The share price dropped wiped hundreds of billions of dollars from the value of Nvidia.
items.text: Hundreds of billions of dollars have been wiped off the value of Nvidia after the US chipmaker announced an independent investigation would be carried out into its chief executive's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The tech firm saw its shares fall by about 4% by close of trade on Monday after Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair. Nvidia's probe came after reports that the US believed the Nvidia boss had been targeted in an espionage campaign by China. However, China has rejected the claims, with its foreign ministry saying allegations about Chinese spies were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China". Nvidia said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised, but a statement by the firm's board of directors said it would begin an investigation in "light of recent reporting that founder and chief executive Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort". items.text: See My World, an event highlighting the pan-African thought via film, poetry and dance, builds on momentum sparked by local activists and creatives African philosophies including exploring how lessons from the past can shape the present and near future have inspired a film festival coming to Manchester . See My World , a day dedicated to independent creators from across the African diaspora in the north of England, will take place at the Contact theatre on 21 November. The festival is part of See My World’s year-round programme showcasing pan-African arts, culture and events. It reflects the determination among creatives and activists in Manchester to build on the legacy of the 1945 Pan-African Congress in Manchester – which connected luminaries of postwar independence movements with a shared vision of liberation – after last year’s 80th anniversary commemorations . items.headline: Ukraine peace talks resume with 'some flexibility' by warring sides, US officials say
items.blurb: Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are all sending delegation to the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
items.text: Moscow and Kyiv are privately showing "a little bit of flexibility" on the issue of who would controls Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario, US officials have said. The comments came on the eve of the first trilateral talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine since February. Senior officials from Moscow, Kyiv and Washington will meet in Abu Dhabi as the fifth anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine approaches. Jared Kushner - Donald Trump's son-in-law and part of the US delegation alongside peace envoy Steve Witkoff - said the talks would be focused on addressing the "postwar security concerns" of both Russia and Ukraine. "An important part of this process is encouraging all parties to begin thinking seriously about what comes after the war," Kushner wrote on X. But Moscow and Kyiv's positions on ending the conflict in the first place remain far apart. A key area of disagreement between the two involves Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is by now mostly occupied by Russia. items.headline: Verdict delayed in Honduras sex-trafficking case linked to disappearance
items.blurb: Angie Pena's disappearance in 2022 exposed what prosecutors called a sex-trafficking network and state corruption.
items.text: A court in Honduras has delayed a verdict in a sex-trafficking case linked to the 2022 disappearance of Angie Pena, a case that has raised concerns about impunity in transnational crimes. On Monday, Honduras’s judiciary cited the need to review evidence and wait for the return of a court interpreter, who was out of the country. The decision has been delayed until November 20. The verdict was expected that same day. Critics framed the unexpected delay as yet another hurdle in a case that has drawn comparisons to the crimes of the late Jeffrey Epstein, a convicted sex offender in the US accused of running a sex-trafficking ring. Four men, including two US citizens, are on trial for crimes related to Pena’s disappearance four years ago. Harold Green and William James Murdock, both from the US, face human-trafficking charges. Another US citizen, Gary Lee Johnston, and Honduran citizen Gustavo Trejo are accused of criminal association. items.headline: Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children
items.blurb: Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.
items.text: Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history. The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa found the cult leader guilty of the crimes. Prosecutors said Paul Mackenzie and his Good News International church ran ​a Christian doomsday sect whose members were ordered to starve themselves and their children to death to go to heaven before the world ended. His accomplices threatened and beat victims to ensure they followed his orders. The emaciated bodies were found scattered in shallow graves and dumped in latrines. Some had been buried alive. items.text: A woman raped by Jeffrey Epstein says the president of the model agency representing her put her in danger, when he sent her to two photoshoots at the convicted sex offender's Florida beach house. At the time, in 2009, Epstein was serving a jail sentence for sex offences against a minor but was allowed to work each day from his home. "My agency's job was to protect me, and they failed. In fact, they put me in danger. And for that, they should be held accountable," she tells the BBC World Service. Roza was 18 when she was first sent to Epstein's Palm Beach home by MC2 Model Management's US branch, having only arrived in the US from Uzbekistan about a month earlier. MC2's US president at the time, Jeff Fuller, now runs another US model agency called The Source Models. "My agency knew exactly where I was. So Jeff knew exactly where I was going," says Roza. items.blurb: In seven decades of the National Conference, the parallel party meeting was seen as a rare implosion and a visible crack that the Opposition parties could exploit to tilt the balance of numbers against the Omar Abdullah government.
items.text: Farooq Abdullah is back in the saddle after nearly withdrawing from NC, govt. affairs managed by his son CM Omar Abdullah. | Photo Credit: file photo The stand-off between the 17 MLAs of the ruling National Conference (NC) and Kashmir’s first political family, the Abdullahs, has had a rare consequence. It has brought the 89-year-old party patriarch, Farooq Abdullah, back into the saddle to steer the party and shape how the government functions, after he had nearly faded from affairs run entirely by Chief Minister Omar Abdullah. The stalemate began on October 27 with the CM’s Cabinet reshuffle, after which at least three senior party leaders publicly expressed resentment over not being inducted. Later that day, the disgruntled legislators held a meeting, conspicuously in the absence of the Abdullahs, and subsequently submitted a charter of demands to the party leadership, which included intensifying the struggle for the restoration of Statehood and special status, removing Nasir Aslam Wani as the CM’s Adviser and reassigning the Roads and Buildings portfolio, currently held by Deputy CM Surinder Choudhary. items.headline: 12 killed in separate overnight Madhya Pradesh fires
items.blurb: Police said an earthen lamp may have triggered the Katni fire, while the Seoni blaze is under investigation.
items.text: Six members each of two families were killed in separate incidents of fire in Katni and Seoni districts of Madhya Pradesh during Diwali celebrations early on Monday, police said. In Katni, an earthen lamp triggered a massive blaze inside a three-storey building, killing six people across three generations, including a two-month-old infant who was found dead in his mother’s lap. According to police, the deceased were identified as Puran Agrawal (77), his wife Chandrakala (74), daughter-in-law Poonam, and granddaughters Arya (14), Anvi (6), and the infant. Two people managed to escape, an official said. Katni superintendent of police (SP) Abhinav Vishwakarma said the fire broke out on the upper floors, situated above a crockery shop. “Preliminary investigation and survivors informed police that a fire started from an earthen lamp kept near a coffee machine and later spread quickly through the house,” he said. Meanwhile, a second fire broke out at a gold trader’s house in Seoni, killing six members of his family. items.headline: Kochi Corporation plans water security assessment to strengthen city’s resilience
items.blurb: The project, which will be implemented with technical support from the Kerala Water Authority, is expected to be completed in six months
items.text: The multipronged project will address water scarcity and pollution, besides focussing on canal rejuvenation and flood mitigation. A water security assessment project is being planned for the Kochi Corporation to strengthen the city’s water resilience. The multipronged project, being developed by Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Palakkad, will address issues, including water scarcity and pollution, besides focussing on canal rejuvenation, sewage management, and flood mitigation. The project, which will be implemented with technical support from the Kerala Water Authority (KWA), is expected to be completed in six months. Once completed, the project is expected to provide a comprehensive framework to guide the planning and implementation of water security projects in the city, said Athira P., associate professor, Department of Civil Engineering, IIT Palakkad. “Different parts of Kochi face specific issues, be it frequently interrupted water supply, flooding, pollution or an increase in the reporting of water-borne diseases. Water security in a region is assessed based on aspects such as water quality and quantity, water-related disasters and ecological factors. items.blurb: Sonia Gandhi blames PM Modi's sharp comments on Jawaharlal Nehru on his “conditioning” by the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS).
items.text: For over a decade, they were top political adversaries, squaring off on India’s electoral battlefield. Yet, in her 544-page memoir, former Congress chief Sonia Gandhi reveals she has had very little real contact with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while acknowledging some common ground with the Bharatiya Janata Party leader. “To this day, I’ve had practically no real contact with him. We meet at semi-official gatherings-for instance, at the Speaker’s chamber,” she writes in her memoir Belonging , which hits the bookstores on Tuesday. “When he comes face-to-face with me, we greet each other with a formal namaste. This is different from the past, when leaders across party divides would treat one another with cordiality. He tends to look away, avoiding eye contact.” She acknowledges that their ideologies and world view are different. “He was fighting for his vision of India, and I for mine: an India against hegemony, an India that stands for inclusiveness, secularism, and social justice. items.headline: Delhi pollution monitors went dark as AQI surged on Diwali
items.blurb: DPCC data showed a peak of 3,744 and a worst-hour average of 1,480, suggesting the official AQI understated the pollution.
items.text: PM2.5 readings, which capture levels of smoke, at many of Delhi ’s air monitoring stations went blank on Diwali night as they climbed towards 1,000 micrograms per cubic metre, pulling down the capital’s official air quality index ( AQI ) for the day after, HT’s analysis of records kept by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) shows. The missing hours, filled partially by on Monday evening by the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC), one of the three agencies that run the stations, show the smoke reaching a peak level of 3,744 µg/m³, more than 60 times the national 24-hour standard of 60. CPCB did not explain the outage. A Delhi government official, who asked not to be named, acknowledged a glitch but gave no details: “The air quality monitors are giving hourly data. There were some technical glitches but all our 43 stations are giving data.” While the PM2.5 data was missing, the stations were still working. items.blurb: Investors are still waiting for Yes Bank to restore their ₹8,415 crore AT-1 bond investments nearly a month after the Supreme Court overturned the 2020 write-off.
items.text: Nearly a month after the Supreme Court overturned Yes Bank’s ₹ 8,415-crore additional tier-I (AT-1) bond write-off, investors who lost their savings are still waiting for the bank to clarify when and how their money will be restored. For Kailash Mishra, the ₹ 10 lakh he invested in Yes Bank’s AT-1 bonds was money set aside for the future. For Gunjan Gupta’s family, the investment represented years of her father’s savings. And for Lakhvir Kaur, a 69-year-old homemaker, it was the retirement corpus she and her husband had carefully accumulated over decades. The wait has become another chapter in a long financial ordeal, for many. Mishra, a 74-year-old retired professional based in Kolkata, said he had almost given up hope of recovering his investment after years of litigation. The Supreme Court verdict has revived his expectations, but he has heard little from the bank about when the money might be restored. items.blurb: Banks led by JPMorgan Chase & Co. could offer one of the year’s biggest discounts to sell some of the $5 billion in debt for software firm Qualtrics International Inc. that the underwriters were stuck holding a few months ago.
items.text: (Bloomberg) -- Banks led by JPMorgan Chase & Co. could offer one of the year’s biggest discounts to sell some of the $5 billion in debt for software firm Qualtrics International Inc. that the underwriters were stuck holding a few months ago. Bankers have scheduled meetings with investors this week to discuss the sale of nearly $2 billion of debt in the high-yield bond market, according to people with knowledge of the matter. Initial indications are that the debt could be marketed at a coupon of at least 8% and a discounted rate of about 85 cents on the dollar, said the people, requesting anonymity as the talks are private. If a deal was struck at that price, it would represent one of the biggest new-issue discounts for a debt sale in the US high-yield market this year, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. A number of software companies have had to pay high borrowing costs and boost protections to lock in lenders in recent months, as concerns about AI-disruption to their businesses have intensified. items.text: Edtech company PhysicsWallah is using artificial intelligence (AI) to improve operational efficiencies and reduce its workforce requirements, even as it looks to expand through inorganic route — acquisitions. The Noida-based company also continues to face profitability challenges in its offline business, despite the expansion of its Vidyapeeth centres. During its Q2 FY27 earnings call, management confirmed that its total employee count, which stood at around 19,100, and faculty strength of approximately 7,100 declined sequentially in the quarter. The firm attributed the reduction partly to efficiencies from AI across content creation, quality checks, test paper preparation and evaluation. Management said AI now writes around 90% of the company's code. The shift towards automation has also helped contain employee expenses, which declined 2.3% year-on-year in Q2 FY27, excluding ESOP costs. For the first half of FY27, employee expenses were down 2.4% compared to the same period last year. However, PhysicsWallah continues to invest in technology which stood at Rs 104 crore in H1 FY27, compared to Rs 70 crore in the corresponding period last year. items.headline: Claude Code is accidentally exposing secrets all over GitHub
items.blurb: "Do not ask again" prompt leads to passwords, API keys, and more being shared.
items.text: Claude Code is leaking sensitive information on public GitHub instances thanks to a partial oversight in the way its settings files are handled. That’s the finding of AI security researchers at Apiiro, who discovered thousands of secrets , including database passwords, API tokens, and root logins, amid Claude Code settings files embedded in GitHub repositories. The leak stems from the way Claude Code handles user approval for automated shell commands. When a user chooses the “Yes, and don’t ask again” option to approve running a command, that choice gets stored as part of a rule in the local “.claude/settings.local.json” file on the user’s computer. That rule is sometimes coded as a pattern, but the command itself is often written to that settings file as is, including any sensitive information that may be embedded within it. This isn’t really a significant security issue if the settings file stays on the user’s local machine (assuming that machine doesn’t become compromised itself, of course). items.text: As voters went to the polls across the US last week, I was in Ashburn, Virginia, part of what’s known as Data Center Alley—the world’s largest data center hub. It’s also where the backlash now sweeping the country arguably first began taking shape. Driving through it is surreal. Concrete monolithic buildings loom along every major road, with names like Skybox and CloudHQ. It’s accepted wisdom in Big Tech that the war against data centers must be about something bigger than just data centers themselves. Two days after the midterms, OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer, Chris Lehane, wrote that data centers “have become a proxy for public unease about affordability, corporate power, and people losing control over their futures.” It’s a culture war, in other words. But spending a few days in Data Center Alley left me wondering if it’s really the proxy that Lehane describes. I came away convinced that the data center backlash is more about electricity than Big Tech admits. items.blurb: Bitter energy drinks turned out to be ChatGPT-steered poisoning, lawsuit says.
items.text: ChatGPT allegedly helped a North Carolina woman, Cheryl Gates, craft a “personalized plan” to poison her husband, James, after fueling her delusions that he planned to divorce her and leave her with nothing. A grand jury indicted Cheryl Gates on charges of attempted first-degree murder and food contamination in October. About a week prior, the accusations that ChatGPT was a co-conspirator in the attempted murder came in a lawsuit filed in San Francisco County Superior Court that was made public this week. In it, James Gates alleged that OpenAI and Sam Altman failed to employ technical safeguards to shut down Cheryl’s chats even after her queries became “obviously suspicious” and sought advice on how to execute and conceal a homicide. At first, Cheryl told ChatGPT that she was researching poisoning out of fear that her husband might possibly try to kill her—framing her queries as “self-protection.” Coming to the rescue, ChatGPT did not terminate the conversation. items.headline: Anthropic reportedly plans to move forward with IPO plans
items.blurb: The AI company is expected to set its valuation range this week, the Wall Street Journal reported.
items.text: Launching a major tech IPO would seem risky right now, shortly after one of Nasdaq’s biggest sell-offs and amid revelations that a CEO central to the AI boom had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. But that isn’t deterring Anthropic, which is moving ahead with its listing plans, according to The Wall Street Journal . Anthropic plans to set a valuation range this week and begin trading on Thursday or Friday of next week, the Journal reported. Investors will look to Anthropic’s valuation to gauge the strength of the AI boom. Some institutional investors are now pushing for a valuation below the $1.5 trillion target discussed as recently as last week, a figure that was itself considerably below the $2 trillion floated a few months ago, the report said. OpenAI, Anthropic’s main rival, was reportedly valued at $1.25 trillion last week after the ChatGPT maker raised $11 billion in fresh capital, short of the $20 billion it had initially sought.

Razorpay is taking a profitability-led pitch to public investors, with its core payments business EBITDA profitable. The 0.4% MDR on large UPI transactions could provide an additional high-margin revenue stream, helping narrow the valuation gap. Analysts estimate MDR could generate ₹192–461 Cr in annual revenue for Razorpay, equivalent to 15–36% of its FY25 gross profit, according to Inc42’s calculations. But the actual upside will depend on revenue-sharing agreements with banks, negotiations with large merchants and how much of its UPI volume qualifies.
